ov: About 1,786 species of soft, leathery, cucumber-shaped echinoderms living on the sea floor worldwide. They recycle nutrients by eating detritus. On the deep sea floor they often make up most of the animal life, and many species are harvested as a delicacy, especially in Asian cuisine.

why.et: A delicacy in Asian cuisines, sold as trepang, namako or bêche-de-mer; some species are farmed.

len: Mostly 10–30 cm; from 3 mm to 3 m
rg: Sea floors worldwide, with most species in the Asia–Pacific region.
df: Detritus and other organic matter on the sea floor.
fx: Deeper than 8,900 m, sea cucumbers make up 90% of the mass of large animal life.
They breathe by drawing water in through the anus into branching “respiratory trees”.
notes: RESOLVED (owner approved all suggestions, 2026-09-29; h left unchanged for bumblebee, hornet and firefly): Group entry. The fact is confirmed: some species expel sticky tubules through a tear in the cloaca ("evisceration") and regrow them in 1.5–5 weeks, and sea cucumbers "eviscerate their gut as a self-defense response".
